note: Draft vectors for LIP-0025. No vector runs a store, an outside record or a clock: states, times and the place where a write stopped are stated. Identities, identifiers of consents and of contracts, commitments in the groups continuity and outside, and block hashes are placeholders. A vector of the groups commitments.entries, continuity, outside and boundaries whose outcome is not the passing one holds one defect and names a neighbour with the passing outcome. A trace states the expected outcome of each step and the state at its end, and names no neighbour.

fields.commitments: chains: an identity and the octets of entries; expect.commitments lists c(0) to c(n). entries: octets and the kind that M1.2 gives them, `no entry`, or `unknown kind`.
fields.continuity: store.commitments maps a position to the commitment that the reader computed for it; store.readable false is a store that cannot be read; outside null is an absent outside record.
fields.outside: record is the outside record before the operation and record_after the record after it.
fields.boundaries: blocks: the time of fencing and a block. first_use: the height of the boundary block, or null where the journal has none, and the height of the block that a parent signs.
fields.consents: journal states the identity and the token of the journal at the start, and whether it has an outside record. Each step has an `op` and its expected outcome. consume: the issuer's steps of M6.3 after the checks of LIP-0020 W7.4 to W7.7, with `now` as the issuer's clock; `crash` says where the write stopped. restart: the continuity check of a starting process. keep and restore: an image of the store is kept and put back. lose: the store is gone. fence: the operator raises the token. start anew: the recovery of M5.3. expect at the end states the identity, the position and the commitment of the store and of the outside record.

rules.title: one atomic write
rules.not_covered: No vector runs a store. The traces state where a write stopped.

rules.title: an entry that the reader cannot read
the four values of the outside record
outside the domain of a restore
rules.not_covered: A property of a deployment. No vector can show where an outside record lives.

rules.title: the outside record never goes back
the act after the outside write
rules.not_covered: The traces state the outcome `consumed` only after the outside write; no vector holds a signature.

rules.title: the other order is another profile
rules.not_covered: No vector holds the other order.

rules.title: restoring
rules.not_covered: trace-05 restores an image that does not pass the check. No vector restores a store that passes it after a loss.

rules.title: one journal for one grant key
the entry of a consumed consent
search and write are one step
rules.not_covered: A trace runs its steps one after another. No vector holds two writers at one moment.

chains.claim: A journal without entries: the commitment at position 0 is the typed digest of the identity.
Two entries. The commitment at position 1 is that of commit-02.
The two entries of commit-03 in the other order: the commitment at position 2 is another one.
The entry of commit-02 in a journal with another identity: every commitment is another one.
The entry of commit-02 with a `consumed_at` that is one second later: the commitment at position 1 is another one.

entries.claim: An entry of a consumed consent, in canonical form.
The members of entry-01 in another order than the canonical one.
An entry of a consumed consent without its `contract`.
An entry of a consumed consent whose `created_at` is a string.
An entry of a kind that this profile does not define. For a reader that does not know the kind, the journal is lost.
Octets that are no JSON object.
An object of more than 2048 octets.

continuity.claim: The identities, the positions and the commitments are equal.
A new journal at position 0 whose outside record holds its first commitment.
The store is one position ahead, and its commitment at the position of the outside record is the commitment of the outside record: a crash between the two writes.
Equal positions and different commitments: two histories at one position. A check of positions alone passes this store.
The store is one position ahead, and its earlier history is not the history of the outside record.
The store is two positions ahead of the outside record.
The store is behind the outside record: what a restore to an earlier position looks like.
The store is empty and the outside record of the same identity stands at position 3: an empty store is no new journal.
The store has another identity than the outside record: it was created anew.
The store is intact, and the writer holds an older token than the outside record: another writer is current.
The store is one position ahead, and the writer holds an older token: it does not complete the write.
A writer with an older token sees an old copy of the store beside a newer outside record. That is fenced and not lost: the token is compared before the histories.

outside.claim: An advance from the exact state that the record holds.
The commitment `from` is another one than the record holds.
The position is one behind the record's: a transition that the record took already.
The position is one ahead of the record's: a transition is skipped.
The token is older than the record's.
The token is larger than the record's: only fencing raises the token.
Fencing with the token that the record holds.

blocks.claim: A block of the active chain in a healthy observation whose header time is 7201 seconds later than the fencing.
The header time is exactly 7200 seconds later than the fencing: a block that a node accepted before the fencing can carry it.
The header time is ten minutes later than the fencing.
The block is not on the active chain of the observation.
The observation is not healthy under LIP-0022 section 2.

first_use.claim: The block that the parent signs lies above the boundary: the lost journal can hold no record under that parent.
The block that the parent signs is the boundary block.
The block that the parent signs lies below the boundary.
The journal has no boundary entry yet.

consents.claim: A consent is consumed once. A second attempt with the same consent finds the entry.
A fresh consent of the same recipient for the same contract is another consent.
A crash after the store write and before the outside write. At the restart the write is completed. The consent is consumed and unused, and a fresh one is needed.
A crash before the store write. Nothing was recorded, and the consent is consumed at the next attempt.
The store is restored to an image from before the consent was consumed. The journal is lost, and no consent is consumed until the operator acts.

Two histories at one position. An image is kept between the store write and the outside write; the store goes back to the image before it; another consent is consumed at the same position; the first image comes back. The positions are equal and the journal is lost.
The operator fences the writer. The writer with the old token consumes nothing, and the writer with the new token does.

The store is gone, and the operator starts anew. A consent that was created before the recovery counts as consumed, also one that the lost journal never held; a consent that was created at the second of the recovery counts as consumed; a later one is consumed.
The clock reads less than the `consumed_at` of the last entry.
The time and the age of LIP-0020 W7.8 come before the journal: a consent of 72 hours and one second and a consent from the future write nothing, and a consent of exactly 72 hours is consumed.
A journal without an outside record consumes nothing.
An entry stays after its consent is too old to pass: the age rule refuses the consent before the journal is asked, and the history keeps the entry.
